answer: One knoll per maker carries a stake for every identity it claims, and no maker gets a second knoll. The grove must re-prove pairwise that no two stakes on a knoll share a record, and the maker pays one turn of its spiral for the new stake plus one for each pair now standing. A turn is one epoch of judged work by its oldest head, and the spiral winds once and never unwinds. A newcomer pays one turn; an operator's thousandth stake costs 499,501 turns of that single head, spun one after another.
